name: ToolRet (Tool Retrieval benchmark). Paper title: "Retrieval Models Aren't Tool-Savvy: Benchmarking Tool Retrieval for Large Language Models"
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025 (ACL 2025 Findings), pp. 24497-24524. Also arXiv:2503.01763 (cs.CL/cs.AI/cs.IR), submitted 3 Mar 2025, last revised 26 May 2025.
authors_affiliation: Zhengliang Shi (Shandong University), Yuhan Wang (Shandong University), Lingyong Yan (Baidu Inc.), Pengjie Ren (Shandong University), Shuaiqiang Wang (Baidu Inc.), Dawei Yin (Baidu Inc.), Zhaochun Ren (Leiden University, corresponding author). Primary affiliations: Shandong University (Qingdao, China), Baidu Inc. (Beijing, China), Leiden University (Leiden, The Netherlands).
code_url: https://github.com/mangopy/tool-retrieval-benchmark (official ACL 2025 code; ~211 stars, Apache-2.0, last pushed 2025-12; evaluation + training scripts)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/mangopy/tool-retrieval-benchmark and leaderboard at https://huggingface.co/spaces/mangopy/ToolRet-leaderboard ; demo at https://huggingface.co/spaces/mangopy/ToolRet-demo ; datasets at https://huggingface.co/collections/mangopy/tool-retrieval ; project website https://mangopy.github.io/tool-retrieval-benchmark/
task_domain: tool-use (tool retrieval / tool selection for LLM tool-augmented agents); information retrieval (cs.IR). This is a benchmark paper evaluating IR models on the tool-retrieval step that precedes tool invocation by LLM agents.
problem_setting: Offline, non-interactive, single-stage tool retrieval (plus optional reranking) over a large static tool corpus given a user query, formatted as an MTEB/BEIR-style IR task (query -> target tools as labels). Supervision: query-tool relevance labels collected and standardized from 30+ existing tool-use datasets. The paper argues that prior tool-use benchmarks unrealistically pre-annotate a small set of 10-20 candidate tools per task, whereas real toolsets are massive (e.g., RapidAPI >52k tools, PyPI >600k packages); ToolRet instead requires retrieving from a 43k-tool corpus. It also supports an instructional-IR setting where each query is paired with an LLM-generated instruction. A companion 200k-instance training set (ToolRet-train) is contributed to fine-tune IR retrievers.
what_is_retrieved: tools (tool / API documents). Each retrieval task's labels are the target tool(s); a tool is a unique identifier paired with documentation (name, description, parameters) describing its functionality. Spans web APIs, code functions, and customized-app tools.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed corpus of 43,215 tools (~43k) merged/deduplicated from 34 source datasets. No agent-written growing/episodic memory; the store is frozen for evaluation (authors note they will maintain/update the benchmark over time, but it is not online-growing at inference).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective, but explicitly evaluated for multi-tool completeness: in addition to NDCG@K / Recall@K / Precision@K they report Completeness@K (C@K, adopted from DUMP/Qu et al. 2024), which is 1 only if ALL target tools for a query appear in the top-K and 0 otherwise. ToolRet emphasizes that solving a task often needs a combination of multiple tools (avg ~ multiple targets per task), so recovering the complete needed set is a first-class objective alongside ranking.
retrieval_unit: tool-API document (a single tool / function / app entry). Each unit is one tool identified by a unique id and paired with detailed documentation (avg tool documentation length 174.56 tokens); the retrieval unit is the whole tool document, not a sub-span.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: 43k-tool corpus aggregated, cleaned (deduplication, text normalization), sampled (K-means clustering with NV-Embed-v1 embeddings for task sampling; manual merge of overlapping toolsets), and frozen. Source datasets collected Aug 2023 - Dec 2024 from AI-conference benchmarks (ACL/NeurIPS), IR/NLP resource tracks (CIKM/EMNLP, e.g., ToolLens, AppBench), and open-source platforms (HuggingFace). The ToolRet-train (200k) corpus is likewise offline-induced from ToolACE, APIGen, and ToolBench training splits. No online/test-time growth.
index_structure_topology: Flat (MTEB/BEIR-style) retrieval index: each task is a query against a flat corpus of tool documents; relevance is judged independently per tool. The benchmark additionally provides a format-based categorization of tools/tasks into three subsets (Web APIs, Code Functions, Customized Apps) for analysis, but this is a partitioning for reporting, not a hierarchical/graph retrieval topology. No dependency graph or category->tool tree is used for retrieval.
retriever_type: Benchmark evaluates multiple types (BM25 sparse, dense single-task retrievers, multi-task embedding models, LLM-based embedding models, and re-ranking models) -> hybrid coverage across six model categories. ToolRet itself is model-agnostic (a benchmark). The contributed fine-tuning recipe (ToolRet-train) trains dense embedding / instruction-tuned retrievers via contrastive learning.
retriever_learning_signal: For the benchmark: none for off-the-shelf models (BM25, MS-MARCO-trained dense models, multi-task embedders are evaluated as-is). For the contributed ToolRet-train fine-tuning: contrastive on similarity labels - each query paired with target tools (positives) and 10 hard negatives retrieved by NV-Embed-v1; the IR model is optimized by maximizing log-likelihood of target tools over positives+negatives (InfoNCE-style softmax over sim(I (+) q, tool)), with K=10 negatives and learning rate 5e-5. Instruction is concatenated to the query with a special token during training. No RL or interactive-preference signal.
query_construction: Raw user query, optionally augmented with an LLM-generated instruction (instructional-IR setting). Instructions are produced by a target-aware strategy: 3 human experts handcraft 100 seed instructions, then GPT-4o generates an instruction per task via in-context learning (sampling seed + generated examples for diversity); the instruction bridges query intent and target-tool functionality (e.g., 'Given an <audio transcription> task, retrieve tools that process audio inputs to produce accurate textual transcriptions...'). Two evaluation settings: w/o inst. (query only) and w/ inst. (query (+) instruction). Queries are not decomposed into sub-queries.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at retrieval time): one query (optionally with one instruction) per retrieval task; no step-level, trajectory-level, or two-level query construction.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (single retrieval pass per query), optionally followed by a single reranking pass for the re-ranking model category.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule / not applicable as a dynamic trigger: retrieval is performed exactly once per query in a standard retrieve(-then-rerank) IR protocol; there is no uncertainty/confidence-based trigger, reflection token, or agent-initiated retrieval request (the agent's end-to-end pass rate is measured downstream but retrieval timing is fixed).
reranking: Yes - re-ranking models form one of the evaluated categories. Cross-encoder / LLM-based rerankers (MonoT5 / castorini/monot5-base-msmarco, jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual, BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-gemma, BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3, mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-large-v1) re-rank the top candidates from a first-stage retriever (e.g., NV-Embed-v1). Key finding: reranking gives limited or even negative gains (MonoT5 reranking NV-Embed-v1 candidates DROPS avg NDCG@10 from 33.83 to 28.92).
retrieved_context_refinement: rerank only (optional). The benchmark protocol applies an optional cross-encoder / LLM reranking stage over first-stage candidates; no decompose-then-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of retrieved tools is part of the benchmark.
how_retrieved_used: (1) As the end task being measured (ranked list of tools, scored by intrinsic IR metrics). (2) Downstream: retrieved top tools are fed as the candidate toolset (prompt augmentation) to tool-use LLMs (GPT-3.5, ToolLLaMA) which then select/invoke tools; the paper measures how retrieval quality changes the end-to-end task pass rate. (3) The 200k ToolRet-train data is used as a training signal to fine-tune IR retrievers.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-act / retrieve-then-plan as a gateway: tool retrieval is the initial step that supplies the candidate toolset to a downstream tool-use agent; the benchmark evaluates retrieval in isolation and also measures its effect on the agent's end-to-end pass rate (pilot study on ToolBench shows replacing officially annotated tools with retrieved tools substantially drops agent performance). No MCTS/tree-search or per-step interleaved retrieval is part of the benchmark.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-query (one retrieval pass per task, optionally one rerank pass); no per-CoT-step, per-sentence/token, or per-tool-call interleaving within a rollout.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw structured tool documentation: each retrieved item is the tool's documentation as text (name, description, parameters/JSON-style fields), e.g., the 'availability' tool doc with parameters. Not a distilled strategy, free-text workflow, executable program, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single tool documentation entry (a tool/API description). It is a single retrievable item (one tool), more concrete than a distilled strategy or reusable workflow; the unit is the functional documentation of one executable tool.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Benchmark-level rather than method-level. (1) Quality control of construction: human-expert review of generated instructions (5 experts, Cohen's Kappa 0.743; 90.1% relevant, 92.3% describe target-tool features, 5.9% hallucination) with revision of low-quality instructions. (2) The paper discusses the one-to-many / overlapping-functionality risk (similar tools across merged datasets) and argues evaluation remains reliable because real-world scenarios pick the single most appropriate tool and tools differ in fine-grained parameters/scope. The contributed training recipe uses hard negatives (NV-Embed-v1-mined) to teach fine-grained discrimination. No retriever-aware distractor-SFT or self-reflection relevance evaluator is proposed.
memory_type: none (static tool corpus; no episodic / skill-library / workflow / procedural / graph / latent memory that grows from agent experience).
write_back: No. ToolRet is a frozen evaluation benchmark; the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills at inference. (The only 'writing' is offline corpus/training-set construction and the authors' stated intent to manually update the benchmark over future versions.)
online_growth: No. The retrievable corpus is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow during deployment/test time (the authors note manual maintenance/updates across benchmark versions, but not automatic online growth).
write_back_trigger: Never (no runtime write-back). Corpus and training data are built once offline (collection -> cleaning -> sampling -> instruction generation -> human validation); no task-success/failure/reflection event triggers a write at inference.
failure_experience_usage: Success-oriented / not applicable for memory. No storage or retrieval of failed agent trajectories. In the ToolRet-train fine-tuning recipe, hard NEGATIVE tools (mined by NV-Embed-v1) are used as contrastive negatives, but these are negative documents for contrastive learning, not stored failure experiences.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only at construction time (datasets merged, deduplicated, normalized into the corpus; benchmark intended to be appended/updated across versions). No post-deployment mutation, dedup-merge at runtime, delta-update, or forget-prune of stored entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No (not an RL / learned-policy retrieval). Retrieval is standard similarity-based top-k (off-the-shelf or contrastively fine-tuned dense/sparse retrievers) with optional cross-encoder reranking; selection is not a sequential decision policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. A single shared static corpus is consumed by individual retrievers/agents; no multi-agent or cross-framework experience sharing.
benchmarks: ToolRet (this paper): 7,615 retrieval tasks (Web API 4,916; Code Function 950; Customized App 1,749) over a 43,215-tool corpus (Web API 36,978; Code Function 3,794; Customized App 2,443); avg query/instruction length 46.87/43.43 tokens, avg tool doc length 174.56 tokens. Aggregated from 30+ (34 merged) existing tool-use datasets, e.g., ToolBench, ToolACE, APIGen, COLT, ToolEyes, AppBench, ToolLens, etc. Companion training set ToolRet-train: 205,826 tasks (avg 2.31 target tools, 5 negatives/query). Downstream agent eval on ToolBench (pass rate). Comparison/reference IR benchmarks: MTEB, BEIR, HotpotQA, MS-MARCO, Natural Questions.
benchmark_family: tool (tool retrieval): ToolRet. Built on tool-use source datasets including ToolBench, ToolACE, APIGen, COLT, ToolEyes, AppBench, ToolLens. Downstream agent benchmark family: tool (ToolBench).
baselines: Six types of IR models. Sparse: BM25s. Single-task dense (MS-MARCO-trained): gtr (gtr-t5-base/large), contriever (contriever-msmarco), colbertv2.0, plus COLT (an ad-hoc tool-retrieval-trained model). Multi-task embedding models: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, e5-small/base/large-v2, bge-base/large-en-v1.5, gte-base/large-en-v1.5. LLM-based / instruction-tuned embedding models: e5-mistral-7b-instruct, gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct, NV-Embed-v1, GritLM-7B. Re-ranking models: MonoT5 (monot5-base-msmarco), jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual, bge-reranker-v2-gemma, bge-reranker-v2-m3, mxbai-rerank-large-v1. Downstream tool-use LLMs: GPT-3.5, ToolLLaMA.
key_metrics: Intrinsic IR metrics at K (mainly K=10): NDCG@K (N@K, ranking quality), Recall@K (R@K), Precision@K (P@K), and Completeness@K (C@K from DUMP; 1 iff all target tools are in top-K else 0). Reported per subset (Web / Code / Customized) and averaged, under w/o inst. and w/ inst. settings. Downstream: end-to-end task pass rate of tool-use LLMs (GPT-3.5, ToolLLaMA) on ToolBench.
headline_result: Even the best model NV-Embed-v1 - strong on conventional IR benchmarks - achieves only NDCG@10 = 33.83 (Avg.) on ToolRet, revealing that retrieval models are not 'tool-savvy'. Low retrieval quality degrades the downstream tool-use LLM pass rate (positive correlation between Recall@10 and agent pass rate). Reranking helps little or hurts (MonoT5 re-ranking NV-Embed-v1 drops avg NDCG@10 33.83 -> 28.92). Fine-tuning IR models on the contributed 200k ToolRet-train substantially improves NDCG@10 and lifts downstream pass rate for both GPT-3.5 and ToolLLaMA.
ablations: (1) Two settings w/o inst. vs w/ inst.: all IR models improve when the query is paired with the generated instruction; instruction-tuned embedders (NV-Embed-v1, e5-mistral) gain the most, evidencing the value of instructions + instruction-following capability. (2) Reranking ablation: cross-encoder/LLM rerankers give limited or negative gains - MonoT5 lowers avg NDCG@10 from 33.83 to 28.92; mxbai-rerank shows a similar trend; bge-reranker-v2-gemma yields only +4.7% Completeness@10. (3) ToolRet vs conventional IR (MTEB) correlation analysis (Fig. 5): the two benchmarks share a trend but ToolRet is harder, attributed to lower query-tool lexical (ROUGE-L) overlap and a task shift from information-seeking to tool retrieval. (4) Training ablation: removing the instruction I from the contrastive loss still beats non-tuned counterparts but underperforms the instruction-tuned version, validating instructional training data. (5) Complexity analysis: ToolRet requires recalling more target tools and has lower query-target lexical overlap than HotpotQA/MTEB, demanding stronger semantic representation.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes - strongly decoupled. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (NDCG@10, Recall@10, Precision@10, Completeness@10) are reported separately, and the impact of retrieval on the end-to-end tool-use task pass rate (GPT-3.5, ToolLLaMA on ToolBench) is analyzed separately, with the correlation between retrieval quality (e.g., Recall@10) and downstream pass rate explicitly studied (Figure 1).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics: ranking-quality IR metrics (NDCG/Recall/Precision/Completeness@10) for the retrieval task and end-to-end task pass rate for the downstream agent. No step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or intermediate trajectory-quality metric (the 'process' studied is the retrieval step's effect on the final agent outcome, not per-step reasoning quality).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency-motivated design (data sampling via K-means clustering to make evaluation tractable on large source datasets). Authors frame adapting/fine-tuning IR retrievers (ToolRet-train) as an efficient plug-and-play alternative to re-training tool-use LLMs to memorize tools. No explicit retrieval latency / API-cost / throughput numbers are reported for the benchmark runs. [uncertain on quantitative latency/cost figures]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k evaluation, primarily K=10 (N@10/P@10/R@10/C@10). Motivated by the limited context length of tool-use LLMs, which cannot fit the full 43k toolset, hence the need to retrieve a small top-k candidate set for the agent. Avg query/instruction length 46.87/43.43 tokens; avg tool doc 174.56 tokens. ToolRet-train uses K=10 mined negatives during fine-tuning. No adaptive/precision-driven variable-size selection is proposed.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a benchmark + training-dataset paper, not a survey/taxonomy).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Transformed/aggregated + LLM-augmented construction. ToolRet is built by collecting 30+ (34 merged) existing tool-use datasets (released Aug 2023-Dec 2024) from AI conferences (ACL/NeurIPS), IR/NLP resource tracks (CIKM/EMNLP: ToolLens, AppBench), and open platforms (HuggingFace); standardizing them into MTEB/BEIR-style query->target-tool IR tasks; cleaning (dedup, normalization); data sampling (K-means clustering on NV-Embed-v1 embeddings, one task per cluster, cluster count = min(#queries, toolset size); manual toolset merge to remove overlap); and instruction construction via a target-aware GPT-4o strategy seeded by 100 human-crafted instructions. Final size: 7,615 tasks over 43,215 tools (Web/Code/Customized). Answer verifiability: labeled ground-truth target tool ids per task. Instruction quality validated by 5 human experts (Kappa 0.743). Companion ToolRet-train: 205,826 tasks (avg 2.31 targets, 5 negatives each) from ToolACE/APIGen/ToolBench. Difficulty signal: best model NV-Embed-v1 reaches only NDCG@10 = 33.83 (Avg.), indicating large headroom.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method). [Retrieve] N/A-as-CBR (the paper studies tool Retrieve mechanically but not as CBR), [Reuse] N/A, [Revise] N/A, [Retain] N/A.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is a tool-retrieval benchmark + training dataset.
tool_document_engineering: Minimal / raw documentation on the corpus side: tools are indexed using their original (cleaned, normalized) docstrings/parameters; no synthetic-query augmentation or expanded summaries of tool docs is applied to the corpus. The engineering effort is on the QUERY side: a GPT-4o target-aware strategy generates an instruction per task (seeded by 100 expert-handcrafted instructions) to support instructional retrieval; instructions describe target-tool functionality to bridge query intent and tools.
index_content_separation: No. Each tool is indexed/retrieved with its full documentation; there is no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content (progressive disclosure / SOP-index-then-content) separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static index (offline-built, frozen per benchmark version; authors plan periodic manual updates). No live tool synchronization and no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling auto-sync CRUD integration; downstream tool invocation is via the source datasets' protocols (e.g., ToolBench/RapidAPI-derived tools) but the benchmark index itself is not live-synchronized.
tool_dependency_awareness: No. Retrieval scores each tool independently; no inter-tool dependency modeling (no dependency graph, bipartite KG, or dependency-aware reranking). Completeness@K measures whether all needed tools are retrieved, but prerequisite/output-feeds-input relations between tools are not modeled.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR case adaptation). Retrieved tools are passed verbatim as candidate documents/toolset to the downstream agent; there is no inference-time adaptation/revision of retrieved items.
builds_on: Standardizes onto IR benchmark conventions BEIR and MTEB (task format) and instructional-IR work (FollowIR / Weller et al. 2024, MAIR/Sun et al. 2024, Asai et al. 2022 task instructions). Uses Completeness@K from DUMP (Qu et al. 2024). Aggregates and reuses source tool-use datasets: ToolBench (Qin et al. 2023), ToolACE (Liu et al. 2024), APIGen (Liu et al. 2024), COLT (Qu et al. 2024), ToolEyes, AppBench, ToolLens, etc. Evaluated retrievers build on NV-Embed-v1, GritLM, e5-mistral, gte-Qwen2, BM25s, ColBERTv2, GTR, Contriever; instruction generation via GPT-4o.
contrasts_with: Prior tool-use benchmarks that simplify retrieval by manually pre-annotating a small (10-20) candidate toolset per task (ToolBench, ToolACE, StableToolBench, Toolink) - ToolRet instead retrieves from a 43k-tool corpus. Also contrasts with ad-hoc tool retrievers trained on narrow tool-use datasets (COLT) lacking systematic cross-scenario evaluation, and with conventional information-seeking IR benchmarks (MS-MARCO, Natural Questions, HotpotQA, MTEB/BEIR) which have higher lexical overlap and single-document targets.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): tool-retrieval benchmark line. It is the first large-scale, MTEB/BEIR-style tool-retrieval benchmark and a foundational evaluation/training resource for the 2024-2025 tool-retrieval sub-topic; downstream work (e.g., Tool-DE / Tool-Embed / Tool-Rank, document-expansion methods) builds directly on the ToolRet corpus and metrics. Lineage: classic IR benchmarks (BEIR/MTEB) + instructional IR (FollowIR/MAIR) applied to tool retrieval, sitting upstream of tool_document_engineering and dynamic-index/MCP tool-retrieval works.
